At PetZone Mahalaxmi Veterinary Clinic, we are dedicated to the health and well-being of your beloved pets. Knowing when to seek immediate veterinary attention can make all the difference in emergency situations. Here are some critical warning signs that indicate your pet may require urgent care:

2. **Sudden Lethargy**: If your pet suddenly becomes unusually tired or inactive, it could be a sign of a serious underlying condition.

3. **Refusal to Eat for More Than 24 Hours**: A sudden loss of appetite, especially when prolonged, can indicate different health threats.

4. **Seizures**: Whether single or multiple, seizures are a medical emergency requiring prompt attention.

5. **Bloating**: Noticeable swelling in the abdomen can signal an emergency, such as gastric dilatation-volvulus in dogs.

6. **Ingestion of Toxins**: If you suspect your pet has ingested something toxic, seek help immediately.

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We trusted this clinic with our 2-year-old cat during the most critical time of his life, and today we are left with heartbreak, trauma, and serious doubts about the care he received.

Our cat was already battling pleural effusion/FIP-related illness, but after the second drainage procedure done at this clinic, his condition worsened dramatically. Unlike the first drainage done elsewhere after which he breathed better and stabilized this time he developed pneumothorax and his breathing never improved afterward.

We were never properly prepared for how unstable his condition had become post-procedure. We also specifically informed the staff that our cat became extremely frightened and aggressive when touched without us present, and requested that he not be unnecessarily handled while we briefly stepped out. Despite that, he was taken out and handled. When we returned, we were met with his lifeless body.

Maybe no one can say with certainty what would have changed the outcome. But as pet parents who watched the drastic difference between the first and second procedures, we cannot ignore the feeling that mistakes, inadequate handling, or complications during treatment may have contributed to his final deterioration.

Losing a pet is devastating enough. Being left with unanswered questions and guilt afterward makes it even harder.

I hope this clinic learns to communicate more transparently, handle critical patients more carefully, and show greater sensitivity toward animals who are already terrified and struggling to survive.

आपत्कालीन मदत असो किंवा यशस्वी उपचार — जानेवारी महिना उत्कर्ष अ‍ॅनिमल हॉस्पिटलमधील विश्वासार्ह पशुवैद्यकीय सेवेचा ठसा उमटवणारा ठरला.
आमच्यासाठी आकडे म्हणजे फक्त संख्या नाहीत — ती वाचवलेली आयुष्ये आहेत.

Animals have rights too—and it is our responsibility to know and uphold them.
Animal welfare laws are designed to protect animals from cruelty, neglect, and abuse, ensuring they live with dignity and care. When we are informed about these laws, we become stronger voices for those who cannot speak for themselves.

Know a few important animal welfare rules in India:
• Causing cruelty, injury, or abandonment of animals is a punishable offence under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.
• Feeding or caring for community animals is legal and protected.
• Injured or sick animals must be given timely medical care.
• Animals have the right to food, water, shelter, and freedom from pain and fear.

Being aware is the first step towards action. Let’s stand together as responsible citizens and create a safer, more compassionate society for all living beings.

प्राण्यांनाही हक्क आहेत—आणि ते जाणून घेणे व त्यांचे संरक्षण करणे ही आपली जबाबदारी आहे.
प्राणी कल्याण कायदे प्राण्यांना क्रूरता, दुर्लक्ष आणि छळापासून वाचवण्यासाठी तयार करण्यात आले आहेत, जेणेकरून त्यांना सन्मानाने व सुरक्षिततेने जीवन जगता येईल.

भारतामधील काही महत्त्वाचे प्राणी कल्याण नियम:
• प्राण्यांवर क्रूरता करणे, त्यांना दुखापत करणे किंवा सोडून देणे हे प्राणी क्रूरता प्रतिबंधक कायदा, 1960 अंतर्गत गुन्हा आहे.
• रस्त्यावरील किंवा सामुदायिक प्राण्यांना अन्न देणे व काळजी घेणे कायदेशीर आहे.
• जखमी किंवा आजारी प्राण्यांना त्वरित वैद्यकीय उपचार देणे आवश्यक आहे.

Animal Birth Control isn’t just about animals—it’s about creating healthier communities and ensuring humane, long-term care.
ABC programs help control stray populations ethically, reduce conflicts, prevent the spread of diseases, and improve the quality of life for both animals and people.
Responsible, compassionate solutions begin with awareness and action.

प्राणी जन्मनियंत्रण (ABC) हे केवळ प्राण्यांपुरते मर्यादित नाही—ते निरोगी समाज आणि मानवी दृष्टिकोनातून काळजी घेण्याबाबत आहे.
ABC कार्यक्रमांमुळे भटक्या प्राण्यांची संख्या नैतिक पद्धतीने नियंत्रणात राहते, आजारांचा प्रसार कमी होतो, संघर्ष टाळले जातात आणि माणसे व प्राणी दोघांचेही जीवनमान सुधारते.
जबाबदार आणि करुणामय उपाययोजना जागरूकतेपासून आणि कृतीपासून सुरू होतात.

एनिमल बर्थ कंट्रोल (ABC) सिर्फ जानवरों के बारे में नहीं है—यह स्वस्थ समुदाय और मानवीय देखभाल सुनिश्चित करने का एक ज़रूरी कदम है।
ABC कार्यक्रम नैतिक तरीके से आवारा जानवरों की संख्या नियंत्रित करते हैं, बीमारियों के खतरे को कम करते हैं, टकराव रोकते हैं और इंसानों व जानवरों दोनों के जीवन स्तर को बेहतर बनाते हैं।
जिम्मेदार और संवेदनशील समाधान जागरूकता और सही कदमों से शुरू होते हैं।

True freedom lies in compassion—for people, animals, and our nation.
Celebrating a Republic that cares for all.

खरे स्वातंत्र्य करुणेत आहे—माणसांसाठी, प्राण्यांसाठी आणि आपल्या राष्ट्रासाठी.
सर्वांची काळजी घेणाऱ्या प्रजासत्ताकाचा आज गौरव साजरा करूया.

सच्ची आज़ादी करुणा में निहित है—लोगों के लिए, पशुओं के लिए और हमारे राष्ट्र के लिए।
ऐसे गणराज्य का उत्सव मनाएँ जो सबकी परवाह करता है।

featured_reviews.name: Sameer Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience.💔

I rescued a severely injured stray cat who was left to die on the road. One of his legs was badly damaged, and with genuine intention to save his life, I brought him here hoping he would receive proper treatment.

Instead of focusing on immediate care or suggesting alternate support options, I was asked to pay ₹5,000–₹6,000 upfront, while being told the total treatment could cost around ₹22,000. As someone who tried to help purely on humanitarian grounds, this was extremely discouraging.

I clearly explained my financial situation and honestly said that I could manage only ₹600–₹700 from my side, which was my genuine capacity. Unfortunately, there was no flexibility, no discussion about raising donations through their network, social media, or other sponsors — which I believe NGOs usually do.

If NGOs start asking large amounts from people who rescue and bring injured strays, then many good-hearted people will stop helping animals altogether. This defeats the very purpose of animal welfare.

With a heavy heart, I had no option but to leave the cat there, feeling helpless and guilty, knowing he might continue to suffer.

This experience was emotionally distressing and disappointing.
